subject.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications

question: Should the Gateway MCP loopback endpoint intentionally change id-less valid JSON-RPC method messages from JSON-RPC response bodies to `202` empty responses for spec compliance?
rationale: The implementation matches JSON-RPC/MCP contracts, but it is still an externally observable behavior change for loopback clients that currently send methods without `id`.

options.title: Accept Spec-Aligned Behavior
options.body: Proceed once real loopback proof is added, accepting the no-response notification behavior as the correct Gateway MCP contract.

options.title: Require Compatibility Guidance
options.body: Ask for docs, migration guidance, or a compatibility policy if existing loopback clients must keep receiving response bodies for id-less methods.

options.title: Pause Protocol Policy
options.body: Hold the PR until Gateway owners define broader raw MCP HTTP request, notification, and batch response semantics.

recommendation.title: Accept Spec-Aligned Behavior
recommendation.body: Proceed once real loopback proof is added, accepting the no-response notification behavior as the correct Gateway MCP contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored and recently reviewed the central Gateway MCP loopback surface, including the adjacent merged raw MCP HTTP hardening work.
